themes.name: Type of offensiveness
themes.description: What in the content itself the participant pointed to as grounds for their decision.

themes.name: Patterns of behavior
themes.description: Reasoning about how often offensive messages occurred across the account, rather than about any single message.

themes.name: Justifications
themes.description: Grounds given for discounting offensive content the participant has already recognised.

themes.name: Reflection on the decision
themes.description: From the observations at the end of section 6.1.3, which the paper reports as falling outside the seven sub-themes. Delete this theme if you would rather not code for these.

themes.name: Decision outcomes
themes.description: When the user talks about banning or suspending, or alternative decisions, codes within this theme are about specific mentions of decisions.

themes.name: Positive content
themes.description: When reviewer recognizes that the comments are positive, happy, uplifting, etc. This is different than the absence of offensiveness.

codes.name: No offensive content
codes.definition: States that the messages reviewed contained nothing offensive.
codes.inclusion: The participant characterises what they read as harmless, friendly, or inoffensive.
codes.exclusion: Not for cases where offensive content is acknowledged and then discounted — use One-off offensive, or a code under Justifications.
codes.example: All the messages I viewed were friendly, therefore I decided not to suspend.

codes.name: Threats of violence
codes.definition: Points to an explicit threat to harm or kill someone as grounds for the decision.
codes.inclusion: Direct threats, wishing serious harm on someone, or references to violence in real life.
codes.exclusion: If the threat is named and then dismissed as venting or a joke, apply Appeal to intent as well.
codes.example: The first message was a clear threat to kill someone.

codes.name: Hate speech and offensive language
codes.definition: Points to slurs, derogatory language, hate speech, or targeted personal attacks.
codes.inclusion: Slurs and identity-based attacks (homophobic, racist, sexist), personal attacks on appearance, insults aimed at someone's family.
codes.example: Using slurs against LGBTQ individuals shouldn't be tolerated.

codes.name: Consistent offensive behavior
codes.definition: Points to a repeated pattern of offensive messages across the account.
codes.inclusion: Counts or proportions of offensive messages, or characterisations such as 'numerous' or 'every comment'.
codes.example: Four out of five comments were offensive enough to suspend.

codes.name: One-off offensive
codes.definition: Treats offensive content as isolated, and therefore as insufficient grounds for suspension.
codes.inclusion: Acknowledges an offensive message while stressing that the remaining messages were fine.
codes.exclusion: Not for accounts the participant describes as having no offensive content at all — use No offensive content.
codes.example: Only one message was offensive among the rest, so no suspension.

codes.name: Contextual understanding
codes.definition: Appeals to context: that the content was misread, that it was normal for the setting, or that more context would be needed to judge.
codes.inclusion: Reading content as banter, treating the situation as not serious enough, or saying the intent cannot be judged without more context.
codes.example: Although a comment seemed offensive, it was part of normal banter.

codes.name: Appeal to intent
codes.definition: Interprets the poster's intent or state of mind — humour, venting, a difficult period, or the capacity to change.
codes.inclusion: Attributing the message to a mood or motive rather than to character, or extending the benefit of the doubt.
codes.example: The user's intention seems more humorous than harmful.

codes.name: Expressed uncertainty
codes.definition: Reports a lack of confidence in the decision that was just made.
codes.example: I wasn't 100 percent confident on my decision.

codes.name: Would revise the decision
codes.definition: On reflection, says they would now decide differently.
codes.example: Looking back now, I think I should've suspended this account.

codes.name: References the recommendation
codes.definition: Mentions the AI or crowd label as a reason for the decision. The paper reports finding no such mentions; the code exists so that absence can be demonstrated rather than assumed.
codes.inclusion: Any reference to what the AI said, or to what other people thought.
